raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Replaces materialized index permutations in `DatasetSampler` with memory-constant,
RNG-backed permutations based on a Feistel network (`rng.FeistelPermutation`, cycle-walking for
non-power-of-two ranges). This keeps memory usage flat for very large datasets.

## Changes

- `rng.py`: `FeistelPermutation` and helpers.
- `DatasetSampler`: uses the RNG permutation for all slice modes.
- `Sharder`: compact range-based slice offsets for `max_samples_per_sequence=1`.
- `compatibility.md`: documents the permutation as part of the iteration-order surface.

## Compatibility

- `ITERATION ORDER BREAKING CHANGE`: shuffled slice order changes for a fixed seed.

## Tests

- New `test_dataset.TestDataset.test_max_samples_per_sequence_one_uses_compact_indexes`;
  expected orders in existing tests updated.

## Validation

- Full unit test suite on this layer: 141 tests passed (CPU).
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, license headers: clean.
- Sphinx docs build (`-E -a`): no warnings.

### 🟡 Changes recommended Checkpointing emits repeated warnings, and the new test does not deterministically release persistent loaders.
2 open findings - [Avoid warnings when checkpointing SliceIndex state](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-Energon/pull/280#discussion_r4257120357) · New - [Ensure persistent loaders are closed deterministically](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-Energon/pull/280#discussion_r4257120419) · New
What changed in this PR Introduces memory-constant Feistel permutations for dataset slice shuffling and compact single-sample slice offsets. **Changes:** - Adds cycle-walked Feistel permutations backed by worker RNG state. - Refactors sampler state and sharding to avoid materialized indexes. - Updates compatibility documentation and expected iteration orders. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `src/​megatron/​energon/​rng.py` | Implements Feistel permutations. | | `src/​megatron/​energon/​flavors/​common/​dataset_sampler.py` | Uses compact permutation state. | | `src/​megatron/​energon/​flavors/​common/​manifest/​sharder.py` | Produces range-based offsets. | | `tests/​test_dataset.py` | Tests compact offsets and restoration. | | `tests/​test_crudedataset.py` | Updates expected shuffled order. | | `docs/​source/​internals/​compatibility.md` | Documents iteration-order compatibility. |
🧠 **Review effort:** Balanced --- 💡 Add a `code-review` agent skill or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. Learn more in the docs.

Saving a mid-epoch state now passes a non-`Savable`, non-builtin `SliceIndex` through `SavableDataset.save_state`, so every checkpoint emits the `UserWarning` from `base_dataset.py:323-330`. Since multi-worker loaders checkpoint repeatedly, this can continuously pollute logs. Please serialize the index data as builtin state or add explicit `SliceIndex` save/restore handling (including the `None` initial state).

This test creates a persistent two-worker loader, and the restored loader below, without closing either one. The iterators are also left suspended immediately after their last requested batch, so cleanup relies on GC and can leave worker processes and `GcDataset` cleanup active when an assertion fails. Use context managers or a `finally` block to close both loaders deterministically.

### 🟡 Changes recommended A mismatched helper name breaks dataset iteration, and checkpoint incompatibility is not fully declared.
2 open findings - [Replacing pending slice state breaks restoration of existing checkpoints](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-Energon/pull/280#discussion_r4259189794) · New - [Dataset iteration calls undefined _pop_pending_slice helper](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-Energon/pull/280#discussion_r4259189868) · New
2 resolved since last review - [Avoid warnings when checkpointing SliceIndex state](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-Energon/pull/280#discussion_r4257120357) - [Ensure persistent loaders are closed deterministically](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-Energon/pull/280#discussion_r4257120419)
🧠 **Review effort:** Balanced

The compatibility impact is broader than the documented in-progress permutation concern: this PR replaces the saved `_pending_slice_indexes` field with `_pending_slices_seed`, while `SavableDataset.restore_state` requires every current `_savable_fields` key (`base_dataset.py:349-350`). Thus every checkpoint produced before this change fails restoration, including epoch-boundary checkpoints. The PR currently declares only an iteration-order break; either add an old-state migration/test or explicitly declare and explain the checkpoint-breaking change as required by this document's compatibility policy.

`_slices_iter` calls `_pop_pending_slice` here and again when a slice is exhausted, but this is the only helper definition and it is named `_next_pending_slice`. Every non-empty dataset iteration therefore raises `AttributeError` before yielding a sample. Rename the helper (or both call sites) consistently.

@@ -48,9 +48,15 @@ Important building blocks include:
 
 - `WorkerRng`, whose state is saved and whose discrete choice avoids depending on changing framework
   implementations;
+- `FeistelPermutation`, which creates a memory-constant bijection and uses cycle walking for non-power-of-two
+  ranges;
 - worker-to-shard assignment;
 - the number and position of random calls in wrappers and user hooks.
 
+Changing a Feistel round function, number of rounds, seeding, or cycle-walking behavior changes the
+permutation even if every sample still appears once. Treat such a change as iteration-order breaking.
+Checkpoints only store the permutation seed, so it also breaks restoring an epoch in progress.
+
 Avoid incidental RNG calls in logging, validation, or skipped paths. A random decision that affects the
 stream must use saved worker state.

+_MASK64 = (1 << 64) - 1
+_GOLDEN_RATIO64 = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15

+def _mix64(value: int) -> int:
+    """SplitMix64 finalizer used as the keyed Feistel round function."""
+    value = (value + _GOLDEN_RATIO64) & _MASK64
+    value = ((value ^ (value >> 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9) & _MASK64
+    value = ((value ^ (value >> 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EB) & _MASK64
+    return value ^ (value >> 31)

+class FeistelPermutation(Sequence[int]):
+    """Memory-constant pseudorandom permutation over ``range(size)``.
+
+    The Feistel network permutes the next power-of-two domain. Cycle walking maps values outside
+    ``range(size)`` back into the requested domain without losing bijectivity.
+
+    Fewer than eight rounds leave a measurable bias for small sizes (e.g. adjacent inputs staying
+    adjacent too often), hence the default.
+    """
+
+    __slots__ = ("_keys", "_left_bits", "_right_bits", "_size")
+    _keys: tuple[int, ...]
+    _left_bits: int
+    _right_bits: int
+    _size: int
+
+    def __init__(self, size: int, seed: int, *, rounds: int = 8):
+        if size < 0:
+            raise ValueError("Permutation size must be non-negative")
+        if rounds < 4 or rounds % 2 != 0:
+            raise ValueError("Feistel rounds must be an even number greater than or equal to four")
+
+        block_bits = max(2, max(size - 1, 0).bit_length())
+        self._size = size
+        self._left_bits = block_bits // 2
+        self._right_bits = block_bits - self._left_bits
+        self._keys = tuple(
+            _mix64(seed + round_idx * _GOLDEN_RATIO64) for round_idx in range(rounds)
+        )
+
+    def __len__(self) -> int:
+        return self._size
+
+    @overload
+    def __getitem__(self, index: int) -> int: ...
+

+    def __getitem__(self, index: int | slice) -> int | list[int]:
+        if isinstance(index, slice):
+            return [self[item] for item in range(*index.indices(self._size))]
+        if index < 0:
+            index += self._size
+        if index < 0 or index >= self._size:
+            raise IndexError("Feistel permutation index out of range")
+        if self._size <= 1:
+            return index
+
+        value = index
+        while True:
+            value = self._permute_block(value)
+            if value < self._size:
+                return value
+
+    def _permute_block(self, value: int) -> int:
+        left_bits = self._left_bits
+        right_bits = self._right_bits
+        left = value >> right_bits
+        right = value & ((1 << right_bits) - 1)
+
+        for key in self._keys:
+            left, right = right, left ^ (_mix64(right ^ key) & ((1 << left_bits) - 1))
+            left_bits, right_bits = right_bits, left_bits

+        return (left << right_bits) | right

inline_comments.body: Saving a mid-epoch state now passes a non-`Savable`, non-builtin `SliceIndex` through `SavableDataset.save_state`, so every checkpoint emits the `UserWarning` from `base_dataset.py:323-330`. Since multi-worker loaders checkpoint repeatedly, this can continuously pollute logs. Please serialize the index data as builtin state or add explicit `SliceIndex` save/restore handling (including the `None` initial state).

This test creates a persistent two-worker loader, and the restored loader below, without closing either one. The iterators are also left suspended immediately after their last requested batch, so cleanup relies on GC and can leave worker processes and `GcDataset` cleanup active when an assertion fails. Use context managers or a `finally` block to close both loaders deterministically.

inline_comments.body: The compatibility impact is broader than the documented in-progress permutation concern: this PR replaces the saved `_pending_slice_indexes` field with `_pending_slices_seed`, while `SavableDataset.restore_state` requires every current `_savable_fields` key (`base_dataset.py:349-350`). Thus every checkpoint produced before this change fails restoration, including epoch-boundary checkpoints. The PR currently declares only an iteration-order break; either add an old-state migration/test or explicitly declare and explain the checkpoint-breaking change as required by this document's compatibility policy.

`_slices_iter` calls `_pop_pending_slice` here and again when a slice is exhausted, but this is the only helper definition and it is named `_next_pending_slice`. Every non-empty dataset iteration therefore raises `AttributeError` before yielding a sample. Rename the helper (or both call sites) consistently.
